items.title: Find the real question
items.body: Every brief arrives as a feature request. I spend the first days turning it back into a question about people — what someone is trying to be certain of, and what currently makes them doubt it. Research, interviews, journey maps; the output is one sentence the whole team can argue with.

items.title: Model before you draw
items.body: Most product failures are data-model failures wearing a UI costume. Before a screen exists I settle the objects and their states — what a case, a booking, a complaint actually is — because the layout falls out of that and never the other way round.

items.title: Build the frame, then the rooms
items.body: One shell, one navigation model, one pattern for list → record → edit. When the frame is decided, a new screen can be specified by describing its content. This is what lets a small team ship four surfaces that still feel like one product.

items.title: Design in states, not ideals
items.body: Empty, loading, partial, failed, offline, too much data. The state nobody documented is the one that ships wrong, so every component gets drawn in the condition it will actually meet on a mid-range phone on a bad connection.

items.title: Test, and let it hurt
items.body: Preference tests and usability sessions are where opinions go to die. When people tell me the image should be bigger, the hierarchy sharper, the icons separated — I change it, even when the earlier version was more consistent with my system.

items.title: Hand off with the reasoning attached
items.body: Specs, tokens, component states, and the argument for each decision written next to the frame. Work that cannot survive a question in review does not survive the sprint either.
